newsitem.title: USA: CSCE to raise margins on Sept "C" coffee futures.
newsitem.headline: CSCE to raise margins on Sept "C" coffee futures.

text.p: Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Thursday it will raise the margin on the September 1997 coffee "C" contract to $6,500, including a $1,500 spot charge, effective May 28.
The previous margin for September, the second nearby contract, was $6,000, including a $1,000 spot charge.

The margin on the July 1997 coffee "C" contract will remain at $8,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, and the margin on all other coffee contracts will remain at $5,000, the exchange said in a statement.

In addition, straddle or arbitrage transactions require a minimum of $1,500 for customers who are CSCE members or members of the trade. However, the $1,500 spot charge for September 1997 and the $3,000 spot charge for July 1997 are applicable to all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving these months, the exchange said.
For customers who are not exchange members or a member of the trade, margins will be 140 percent above trade rates, CSCE said. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
